# Unify Consulting () - SVP Technical Pre-Sales and Enterprise Solution Architecture briefing packet

## JD Complement
The role likely exists to bridge Unify’s advisory-led selling with delivery-ready architecture in AI-heavy enterprise pursuits. The operating tension is not “build the tech,” but “turn strategic consulting into a credible, implementable,
and partner-aligned solution fast enough to win.”

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Unify Consulting is a services-led management consulting firm with an AI-forward positioning and a stated aim to be a flexible, integrated alternative to large global consultancies. Its motion appears to combine strategy, architecture,
implementation roadmap design, and enterprise change support.

The archetype is hybrid consulting: advisory plus solution shaping plus delivery enablement. That means the company wins by translating business problems into practical operating plans, not by selling a standalone software product.

For this role, the central tension is between high-touch enterprise credibility and repeatable solution framing. The company needs leaders who can make complex pursuits feel bespoke while still using reusable patterns, partner assets, and
implementation roadmaps.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Publicly available company data places Unify in the mid-market consulting tier, with estimates around 501 to 1,000 employees and revenue in the roughly $100M to $170M range. It was founded in 2006 and has been recognized by Business Insider
as one of America’s Top Management Consulting Firms for 2026.

That scale creates a common consulting pressure: preserve senior-client intimacy while expanding AI and data work across more accounts. The role likely helps solve decision-rights friction between sales, architecture, and delivery so
pursuits can move from discovery to credible solution design without losing momentum.

The company’s AI emphasis suggests pressure to stay relevant as clients accelerate AI-driven change. Positioning must therefore show both strategic fluency and practical enterprise execution.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Verified public material does not support naming a detailed org chart. The likely stakeholder map is clear, though: consulting leadership, practice leaders, delivery leads, client partners, and solution architects.

This role probably sits at the intersection of business development and delivery assurance. It would need to align executive sponsors, technical SMEs, and implementation teams around a single solution narrative that can survive procurement,
security review, and handoff.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Unify explicitly markets AI strategy, planning, and operations, and it frames architecture as part of solution design and roadmap development. Its public messaging also emphasizes data engineering and management, analytics modernization,
and turning engineering data into business impact.

The architecture signal is practical rather than research-heavy: select tools, define high-level architecture, and build an implementation roadmap. That implies a need for solution leaders who can connect cloud, data, and operating model
choices to business outcomes.

The company also has a visible cloud-adoption and change-management angle, which matters for enterprise modernization work. The role likely needs to make modernization feel adoptable, not just technically sound.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Verified partner-program detail is limited in the available material, so the safest read is that ecosystem motion is enabling rather than productized. The company’s consulting model suggests it may rely on cloud, data, and enterprise
technology partners to strengthen solution credibility.

For this role, that means partner value is likely in co-shaped solution narratives, reference architectures, and implementation confidence. If partner motion is used well, it can shorten sales cycles by making the proposal feel lower-risk
and more executable.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Recent public signals include the 2026 Business Insider recognition and ongoing publication of AI, cloud adoption, and data-focused thought leadership. Those signals suggest the firm is actively reinforcing its market position around
AI-enabled consulting.

The urgency for this role is likely driven by enterprise buyers demanding faster proof, clearer ROI, and more concrete implementation plans. In that environment, solution architecture becomes a commercial function, not just a technical one.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise consulting that converts strategy into implementation-ready architecture
- AI and data modernization with business-outcome framing
- Pre-sales support that de-risks complex pursuits
- High-trust executive communication in advisory environments
- Cloud and analytics roadmap design for enterprise clients
- Cross-functional handoff between pursuit, architecture, and delivery
- Reusable solution patterns that still feel tailored
- Partner-aware solution shaping in consulting-led sales

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Reference Unify’s AI-management-consulting positioning and ask how they are packaging architecture for faster enterprise pursuits
- Mention the tension between bespoke consulting and repeatable solution roadmaps
- Ask how they are turning AI strategy work into implementation-ready client narratives
- Note the importance of making cloud and data modernization feel adoptable, not just ambitious
- Ask how they align consulting, architecture, and delivery when a deal moves from discovery to validation
- Reference the need for credible ROI language in AI and analytics engagements
- Ask whether partner assets are being used to strengthen solution confidence in enterprise sales

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
